title: Mortgage rates rise, bringing the average rate on a 30-year home loan to where it was 4 weeks ago
summary:
Mortgage rates ticked higher this week, nudging the average long-term U.S. home loan rate closer to its recent high for the year.
The benchmark 30-year fixed rate mortgage rate edged up to 6.66% from 6.65% last week, mortgage buyer Freddie Mac said Thursday.
One year ago, the average rate was 6.56%.
Higher mortgage rates can add hundreds of dollars a month in costs for borrowers, limiting homebuyers' purchasing power.

title: Trump says the US doesn’t need Canada. The economy says otherwise
summary:
TORONTO (AP) — U.S. President Donald Trump says his country does not need Canada.
But every day, roughly 4 million barrels of Canadian crude oil flow south, helping fuel American cars, trucks and airplanes and supply U.S. industry.

title: Have a CD account set to mature this September? Here's where you should (and shouldn't) move your money next.
summary:
If time is running out on your current CD account, it makes sense to start planning your next moves now.
If they opened a certificate of deposit (CD) account in recent months or years, its maturity date could arrive in the month.
Where you should move your maturing CD account money this SeptemberDon't let your maturing CD account money automatically rollover into a new account, especially as that can risk extending your loss of access and, potentially, lock you into an account with a lower interest rate than you're currently earning.
So don't rush to open an account or transfer any money until you've found the right account with the right rate.
The one notable difference, however, is that money market accounts also offer check-writing services that neither a high-yield savings or CD account will.

title: Andy Burnham calls National Economic Council summit with UK nations
summary:
Andy Burnham says he will bring together the leaders of Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland this autumn for a summit to help boost the UK economy.
The first ministers of Wales and Scotland, and the first and deputy first ministers of Northern Ireland will meet Burnham at the National Economic Council in October.
The National Economic Council was created by Gordon Brown's UK government in the wake of the 2008 banking crash, and has now been revived by Burnham.
Plaid Cymru Deputy First Minister of Wales Sioned Williams, speaking before she met Burnham at the visit to the steelworks, said she thought "the announcement about the National Economic Council is a hopeful thing".
"We can discuss challenges there, we can discuss how every postcode, as the prime minister has put it, needs to see economic growth.
